title: Human panel v3: finishing pressure and favorable board attacks, with hand activation restraint

rules.advice: In the main phase, avoid actions with a higher memory cost.
In the main phase, avoid actions that pass more memory to the opponent.
In the main phase, avoid attacks on the opponent's security.
In the main phase, favor attacks on the player at zero opposing security.
In the main phase, favor attacks on opposing Digimon with lower DP.
In the main phase, avoid attacks on an opposing Digimon with equal or higher DP.
In the main phase, favor digivolving.
In the main phase, favor digivolving the Digimon in the breeding area.
In the main phase, favor digivolutions that gain more levels.
In the main phase, favor digivolutions that gain more DP.
In the main phase, favor playing Digimon from hand, more so for higher DP.
In the main phase, favor playing Tamers.
In the main phase, favor using Option cards.
In the main phase, favor actions by higher-level cards.
In the main phase, favor actions by higher-DP cards.
In the main phase, avoid actions that target higher-DP Digimon.
In the main phase, avoid ending the main phase.
In the main phase, favor activating card effects.
In the main phase, avoid actions that use a card from hand.
In the main phase, avoid actions that use a card from the trash.
In the main phase, avoid actions by a Digimon already on the battle area.
In the main phase, avoid actions whose source is an opposing card.
In the main phase, favor actions by more valuable cards (DP, level, and cost combined).
In the main phase, avoid DigiXros plays.
In the main phase, favor Assembly plays.
In the main phase, favor DNA digivolution.
In the main phase, favor App Fusion.
In the main phase, avoid linking cards.
In the main phase, favor actions that use more material cards.
In the main phase, use activated effects that cost no memory before other plays, because they never end the turn and often make the next play cheaper.
Hatch when the breeding area is empty.
Move a developed line out to contest the board.
At zero security, prioritize blocking an attack on the player.
Consider optional effects and defensive responses when their costs are acceptable.
Finish optional selections when additional cards do not improve the outcome.
Keep an opening hand with a rookie that can start your line.
When choosing targets for your own effect among opposing cards, favor the most valuable opposing Digimon (higher DP and level).
When you still have 3 or more security cards, decline ordinary blocks and keep your Digimon; take the security check instead.
In a counter window, favor using a counter card from hand, such as Blast Digivolve, over declining.
Decline a Barrier response when you have 1 or fewer security cards; keeping the last security card matters more than saving the Digimon.
When a card selection picks among opposing cards on the battle area, favor the most valuable opposing Digimon (higher DP and level).
When choosing targets for your own effect, prefer picking a legal target over finishing the selection early.
In the main phase, reduce the preference for activating effects from hand.
